sourceChecks.section: Full-time Law programme, all year1–3 component descriptions, language, legal skills and BSA
sourceChecks.finding: The target is the general Rechtsgeleerdheid bachelor at Erasmus School of Law. Legal sources, interpretation and application organise it, with substantial Dutch private/public/criminal doctrine, legal-academic skills and international/EU law. Published descriptions independently support the component-level judgments. No named specialisation is required.

Articles10–11 confirm the exact23component credit structure,60EC/year,180uniqueEC. All components compulsory except the constrained15ECminor. Both modes exist; choose the ordinary full-time sequence. Dutch is default; three named international/EU components have English exams. The15ECminor must be accessibleEUR provision or an approved coherent external package. Law&Business is one21ECintegrated component, with required participation in two parts,70/30grading, part1minimum5.5; not separately credited child units. SkillsIII is one10ECcomponent: research preparation period2, thesis periods3–4, two preparation assessments15%each, thesis70%, thesisminimum6, allpartscomplete. B3 requires allB1 and42B2EC; minorfrom3rdenrolmentyear. Conditional28B2EC admission for SkillsIII/Law&Business requires42at stated checkpoints. Completing preceding60ECyears meets ordinary progression. No compulsory separate credit-bearing placement or extra invented thesis credits.

sourceChecks.finding: Named later masters and legal/advisory/government/company careers support search-only outcome rows; they are not bachelor tracks or generators. Bachelor plus subsequent master qualification context is retained.

Current officially linked English TER independently confirms the same component/code/credit framework. It retains Dutch component names; readable English display titles are faithful translations, preserved alongside originals internally.

routeSelection: Generic target; no formal route required. English display translations do not change actual teaching language.

alignmentSourceChecks.y3-legal-philosophy: Official description explicitly lists utilitarianism, Kantian duty ethics and virtue ethics, professional ethics, legal pluralism, social contract, rule of law, rights, democracy, injustice, legal moralism, punishment and universalism. Ethics directly addresses its important moral-theory part, not the whole legal-philosophy syllabus. Human Rights instead remains unmatched on its own row because its legal/historical rights scope is not replaced by a generic philosophy equivalence.
alignmentSourceChecks.y1-empirical: Official description explicitly uses sociological, psychological and anthropological methods to investigate law in action. Qualitative Research Methodology is the strongest selected disciplinary-method counterpart, with law-specific application clearly absent. General statistics remains substantive support, not a second duplicate match.
alignmentSourceChecks.y1-law-econ-society: Official description analyses the social-cost function of law and connections among legal fields. Generic economic incentives do not directly implement that primary legal analysis; leave blank.
alignmentSourceChecks.y1-skills and y2-skills: Dedicated legal source use, legal memo/procedural documents, oral legal advocacy, research and responsible digital tools are not interchangeable with general rhetoric/persuasion. Selected law courses exercise related functions but already occupy stronger substantive rows.
alignmentSourceChecks.y2-substantive-criminal: Source-first recheck of official Year2description centres liability/guilt/attempt/participation/defences. UCR211shares exactly this important primary content, so it is a stronger counterpart than the introductory mixed substantive/procedural course. Move the single match; retain first-year intro as explicit gap. Same-AI finding recorded separately.
